Valley Electric Association, Inc. (“VEA”) hereby submits its Motion to Rescind Show 
Cause Order and Conditional Request for Extension of Time (“Motion”). VEA is a non-public 
utility under Section 201(f) of the Federal Power Act and asks the Commission to rescind its June 
18, 2026 show cause order as to VEA, as the Commission has said it will do at a non-public utility’s 
request.1 If the Commission has not acted by November 16, 2026, VEA asks that its time to respond 
be extended. In addition to this filing letter, VEA submits the Motion and a Certificate of Service. 
Respectfully submitted,

II. 
DESCRIPTION OF VEA 
VEA is a rural electric distribution cooperative based in Pahrump, Nevada, with a service 
territory in southern Nevada and a small portion in California.  VEA is generally not regulated by 
the Commission because it is a rural electric cooperative that sells fewer than 4 million megawatt 
hours of electricity per year.   In 2011, the Commission accepted a Transition Agreement between 
VEA and the CAISO that established the process for VEA to join the CAISO as a Participating 
TO.6   
VEA became a Participating TO and a signatory to the Transmission Control Agreement 
(“TCA”) in 2013, placing its 230 kV and 138 kV facilities under the CAISO’s Operational Control. 
In 2017, the Commission approved the acquisition of VEA’s 230 kV system by GLW, a Non-
Load-Serving Participating TO and a respondent in this proceeding.7 VEA’s only remaining 
facilities under CAISO Operational Control are its 138 kV facilities, which are Low Voltage 
Transmission Facilities whose costs are recovered from VEA’s own members.  Interest from large 
loads in VEA’s territory has focused on GLW’s 230 kV system. 
III. 
BACKGROUND 
The Show Cause Order directed the CAISO and its Participating TOs to show cause why 
their tariffs remain just and reasonable without provisions addressing large and co-located loads,

recognized that the Participating TOs “include entities that are not subject to the Commission’s

included them because their TO Tariffs on file describe the wholesale load interconnection 
process, and stated that “[i]f a non-public utility wishes to be removed from this proceeding, we 
will rescind the show cause order against them at their request.”9 
The Six Cities and WAPA moved for rescission of the Show Cause Order on July 31 and 
August 3, 2026. On August 3, VEA joined fourteen other CAISO Participating TOs (collectively, 
the “Joint PTOs”) in a Request for Abeyance asking the Commission to extend each Joint PTO’s 
deadline to respond to the Show Cause Order to November 16, 2026.10 The Commission’s August 
14 Order granted both forms of relief: it rescinded the Show Cause Order as to the Six Cities and 
WAPA as utilities exempt under Section 201(f), and it held the proceeding in abeyance through 
November 16, 2026, suspending the response obligation of any respondent that submits an FPA 
Section 205 filing by that date.11 The CAISO Board of Governors approved the CAISO’s large 
load proposal on October 28, 2026. That proposal preserves the existing allocation of 
responsibilities under which the Participating TOs primarily manage load interconnection studies 
and financing under their own TO Tariffs, and the CAISO expects complementary filings from the 
Participating TOs.12

IV. 
JUSTIFICATION FOR RESCISSION 
A. 
VEA Is Exempt From the Commission’s Jurisdiction Under FPA Section 201(f) 
Section 201(f) excludes from Part II of the FPA “an electric cooperative that receives 
financing under the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 . . . or that sells less than 4,000,000 megawatt 
hours of electricity per year.”13 VEA sells approximately 577,130 MWh’s of electricity per year; 
therefore, it is exempt from Part II of the FPA pursuant to Section 201(f). As the Six Cities did, 
VEA acknowledges the Commission’s authority to review VEA’s Transmission Revenue 
Requirement to ensure that the CAISO’s rates remain just and reasonable.14 
VEA stands in the same position as the Six Cities and WAPA. Each is a non-public utility 
Participating TO with a TO Tariff on file with the Commission, each asked to be removed from 
this proceeding while committing to continue coordinating with the CAISO, and the Commission 
granted each request.15 The same result is appropriate for VEA. The timing of this motion is also 
no obstacle. The Show Cause Order places no deadline on a non-public utility’s request; it provides 
that the Commission will rescind the order “[i]f a non-public utility wishes to be removed from 
this proceeding.”16 
B. 
VEA Will Continue to Coordinate with the CAISO and Remains Subject to the 
CAISO Tariff 
VEA makes the same commitments on which the Commission relied in the August 14 
Order. VEA has coordinated and will continue to coordinate and cooperate with the CAISO in

respect to the load interconnection provisions of its TO Tariff. VEA has conferred with the CAISO 
in advance of this filing and is authorized to state that the CAISO supports this motion. VEA is 
also coordinating with GLW on the respective roles of GLW and VEA in processing large load 
requests in VEA’s territory.   If VEA determines that changes to its TO Tariff are needed to address 
the issues in the Show Cause Order, VEA will file proposed revisions with the Commission. 
Rescission will not diminish the CAISO’s visibility into or authority over large loads in 
VEA’s territory. VEA remains a party to the TCA and will be subject to the large load provisions 
of the CAISO Tariff applicable to Participating TOs. VEA is also the Load Serving Entity and 
Utility Distribution Company for its territory and, through its Scheduling Coordinator, will be 
subject to the forecasting, telemetry, and scheduling requirements that the CAISO Tariff imposes 
for any large load in its territory, wherever that load interconnects.  
C. 
VEA’s Participation in the Joint PTOs’ Request for Abeyance Does Not Alter Its 
Section 201(f) Status 
VEA joined the Joint PTOs’ Request for Abeyance to preserve its ability to coordinate with 
the CAISO and the other Participating TOs and to participate in the CAISO large load stakeholder 
process to develop a common approach to responding to the Show Cause Order. The Joint PTOs 
explained that many of the Commission’s concerns “can only be resolved with complementary or, 
at a minimum, non-conflicting tariff provisions among the CAISO Tariff and the various TO 
Tariffs,” and that their requests “reflect a coordinated regional effort consistent with Commission 
direction.”17 VEA supported that effort and continues to support it. 
 
17 Request for Abeyance at 4, 6.

- 7 - 
The Request for Abeyance stated that each Joint PTO planned to develop an FPA Section 
205 filing to amend its TO Tariff.18 It also recognized, however, that “there are significant 
differences among the California PTOs (some PTOs serve load while others do not, for example) 
such that the appropriate TO Tariff changes to implement the OSC will also likely vary from PTO 
to PTO,” and it described the anticipated filings as matters that “remain under development and 
may evolve through coordination with CAISO and stakeholders.”19 The CAISO large load 
stakeholder process is now complete. The CAISO Board of Governors approved the CAISO’s 
proposal on October 28, 2026, and the Participating TOs will make individual filings tailored to 
their own systems rather than a single joint filing. VEA’s 138 kV facilities neither host nor are 
likely to host a large load, as explained in Section IV.D below. VEA has therefore concluded that 
a Section 205 filing is not warranted and seeks the relief the Commission has already extended to 
the other non-public utility respondents. 
 Nothing in the Joint PTOs’ Request for Abeyance waived VEA’s status under Section 
201(f) or the option the Commission offered non-public utilities in the Show Cause Order. Nor 
does VEA’s participation in the Request for Abeyance foreclose rescission. The Six Cities paired 
their motion to rescind with a conditional request for abeyance, and the Commission granted 
rescission without needing to reach the abeyance request.20

D. 
Large Loads in VEA’s Territory Would Interconnect to GLW’s 230 kV System, 
Which Remains Before the Commission 
The Show Cause Order addresses large loads, which the Commission described as new 
commercial or industrial customers with a peak load of 50 MW or greater that interconnect to the 
transmission system at a voltage above 69 kV.21 Large loads seeking service in VEA’s territory 
likely would not interconnect to VEA’s 138 kV facilities, given the option to interconnect with 
GLW’s more robust 230 kV system. 
Service over those 230 kV facilities is governed by GLW’s TO Tariff, not VEA’s. GLW 
is a public utility, and remains a respondent in this proceeding, The rates, terms, and conditions 
the Show Cause Order addresses for large loads in VEA’s territory will therefore remain before 
the Commission through GLW and the CAISO. Rescinding the Show Cause Order as to VEA 
leaves no gap in the Commission’s review, and the Commission has already stated that it expects 
the CAISO to respond regarding a non-public utility’s CAISO Tariff provisions on file with the 
Commission.22 
V. 
CONDITIONAL REQUEST FOR EXTENSION OF TIME AND WAIVER OF 
ANSWER PERIOD 
Responses to the Show Cause Order are due November 16, 2026, unless the respondent 
has submitted a Section 205 filing by that date.23 Rule 2008(a) provides that the time by which any 
person is required to act under any order may be extended by the decisional authority “for good 
cause, upon a motion made before the expiration of the period prescribed.”24 Good cause exists 
here. The Commission has committed to grant rescission to non-public utilities on request and

here, VEA’s response obligation will be moot. Requiring VEA to prepare a response to a Section 
206 order from which the Commission has said it will remove VEA would serve no purpose. 
Accordingly, if the Commission has not acted on this motion by November 16, 2026, VEA 
requests that its time to respond to the Show Cause Order be extended until thirty days after the 
Commission acts on this motion. This request is of the same character as the conditional abeyance 
motion the Six Cities filed on August 3, 2026, which was expressly conditioned on the 
Commission’s disposition of their motion to rescind and which the Commission found unnecessary 
to address once it granted rescission.25 VEA further requests that the Commission waive or shorten 
any answer period applicable to this motion, as it did for the Six Cities and WAPA motions, so 
that the Commission may act before November 16, 2026.26

VI. 
CONCLUSION 
WHEREFORE, VEA respectfully requests that the Commission (1) rescind the Show 
Cause Order as against VEA as a non-public utility and amend the caption accordingly; (2) if the 
Commission has not acted by November 16, 2026, extend VEA’s time to respond to the Show 
Cause Order as requested above; and (3) waive or shorten any answer period applicable to this 
motion.
